country.comment: National data on urban slums across India, with primary descriptive and multivariable regression analyses restricted to the 10 Indian states with at least 10 sampled slums per survey wave (Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Orissa, Tamil Nadu, and West Bengal).

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative multivariable multilevel linear and logistic regression estimates plus weighted descriptive trends across 1993–2012 NSS waves.
effect_estimate.value: In the primary multilevel linear regression (N = 2,390 slums across 4 NSS waves in 10 states; weighted N = 168,901), each 1-year increase in legal notification is associated with a 0.768-point lower Basic Services Deprivation Score (BSDS, 0–100 scale where higher indicates worse deprivation; beta = -0.768, 95% CI: -0.914 to -0.622, p < 0.001; quadratic term beta = 0.009, 95% CI: 0.005 to 0.013, p < 0.001). Modeled dichotomously, notified slums score 10.546 points lower on BSDS than non-notified slums (beta = -10.546, 95% CI: -12.092 to -9.001, p < 0.001). Slums on central government land have higher deprivation than those on state/city government land (beta = 6.785, 95% CI: 3.480 to 10.089, p < 0.001), whereas slums on private land have lower deprivation (beta = -3.182, 95% CI: -4.880 to -1.483, p < 0.001), and lacking a community association is associated with higher deprivation (beta = 4.291, 95% CI: 2.622 to 5.961, p < 0.001). Between 1993 and 2012 in the 10 states, lack of piped water fell from 37.3% to 16.2% in notified slums while rising from 30.2% to 33.6% in non-notified slums; lack of septic/flush/pour-flush toilets fell from 61.6% to 27.7% in notified slums vs. 62.6% to 57.0% in non-notified slums; and lack of sewer infrastructure fell from 79.1% to 53.8% in notified slums vs. 85.0% to 82.0% in non-notified slums. In 2012 NSS multilevel logistic regression (N = 706 slums; weighted N = 28,635), non-notified slums had lower odds of receiving government slum-improvement financial aid than notified slums (OR = 0.379, 95% CI: 0.246 to 0.584, p < 0.001).
